title: Local Team Wins Thrilling Championship Final
author: Sita Sharma
content:
In front of a packed stadium, the home team secured the championship with a last-minute goal. Fans stayed on their feet through the final minutes as both sides pushed for a winner.

The captain said the win was the result of a full season of hard work and belief in the group. Celebrations continued in the streets late into the night.

title: Young Runners Prepare for Annual City Marathon
author: Ram Thapa
content:
More than two thousand runners have registered for this year's city marathon, the highest number ever. Many first-time participants have been training in local parks for months.

Organizers say water stations and medical tents will be placed every two kilometres along the route.

title: New Programming Course Opens for Beginners
author: Anita Gurung
content:
A free online course aimed at complete beginners has opened enrolment this week. It covers the basics of HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and ends with students building a small website.

Instructors say no previous experience is needed, only a computer and the willingness to practise a little each day.

title: Solar-Powered Buses Begin Test Runs
author: Bikash Rai
content:
Two solar-assisted buses have started trial runs on a busy city route. Engineers say the rooftop panels reduce battery use during the day and help lower running costs.

If the trial goes well, the transport office plans to add more buses next year.

title: Parliament Debates New Education Budget
author: Maya Karki
content:
Lawmakers spent most of the day discussing next year's education budget. Supporters argued that more funds are needed for school buildings and teacher training.

Others asked for clearer reports on how earlier funds were spent before approving any increase. The debate will continue next week.

title: Voters Urged to Check Their Names on the List
author: Sunil Adhikari
content:
Election officials have asked citizens to check that their names appear correctly on the voter list. Corrections can be made at the local ward office until the deadline.

Officials say a few minutes of checking now can avoid problems on voting day.

title: Film Festival Opens With Short Films From Students
author: Pooja Lama
content:
The annual film festival opened this weekend with a special screening of short films made by college students. The films ranged from comedies to documentaries about everyday life.

The audience praised the creativity shown, and organisers said entries doubled compared with last year.

title: Street Musicians Bring Life to Old Market Square
author: Dipesh Shrestha
content:
Every Saturday evening a group of local musicians now plays in the old market square. Shoppers stop to listen, and some join in with clapping and dancing.

The group hopes to turn the weekly gathering into a small music festival during the next holiday season.

title: Community Plants One Thousand Trees in a Day
author: Kamala Joshi
content:
Volunteers of all ages gathered on a hillside this Sunday and planted one thousand saplings in a single day. Schools, clubs and families all took part.

Organisers say volunteers will return each month to water the young trees and check how they are growing.

title: Library Extends Opening Hours for Exam Season
author: Nabin Basnet
content:
The public library will stay open two extra hours every evening during exam season. Students can use the reading rooms and free Wi-Fi.

The librarian said the change was made after many students asked for a quiet place to study after classes.
